title: Restriction along a DG quasi-isomorphism is a derived equivalence
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. Let $\varphi:(A,d)\to(B,d)$ be a homomorphism of differential graded algebras (degree-preserving, unital, multiplicative, commuting with $d$) inducing isomorphisms $H^i(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(B)$ for all $i\in\mathbf Z$. Restriction of scalars $N\mapsto N_A$, which keeps the underlying complex of $N$ and lets $a$ act through $\varphi(a)$, induces a functor $R:D(B,d)\to D(A,d)$; it commutes with shifts and mapping cones on the level of modules, hence is exact. Then $R$ is an equivalence of triangulated categories. It has a left adjoint $L:D(A,d)\to D(B,d)$, the derived tensor product $M\mapsto M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AB$, which is an exact quasi-inverse of $R$: the unit $\mathrm{id}\to RL$ and the counit $LR\to\mathrm{id}$ of the adjunction are isomorphisms, and $L$ carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles with shift comparisons compatible with unit and counit.

proof.text: Give $B$ its $(A,B)$-bimodule structure $ab=\varphi(a)b$. By [lem-sfb-dg-bimodule-derived-adjunction], $L=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ has exact right adjoint $U_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(B,-)$, with compatible shift comparisons. Restriction $R$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms because it leaves the underlying complexes unchanged, and commutes with shifts and cones, so descends as the exact functor stated in the item. For a right DG $B$-module $I$, evaluation $f\mapsto f(1)$ identifies $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(B,I)$ with $I_A$ as DG $A$-modules: its inverse sends homogeneous $x$ to $(b\mapsto xb)$, its differential evaluates to $d_Ix$ since $d_B1=0$, and $(fa)(1)=f(\varphi(a))=f(1)\varphi(a)$. For the homotopically injective resolution $Y\to I$ supplied by the cited node, $Y_A\to I_A$ is still a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the models identify $U_B$ naturally with $R$, including their shift comparisons. Transport the specified adjunction to obtain $L\dashv R$ with exact $L,R$ and shift-compatible unit and counit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dg-finite-cell-compact] to the right DG $B$-module $B$ with filtration $0\subset B$ and quotient the single unshifted copy of $B$. This gives the compactness hypothesis for the bimodule $N={}_AB_B$ in $D(B,d)$.

source.place: Tag 09S6, first sentence of proof, compactness input to Tag 09R9; Tag 09R3, proposition-compact.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dg-free-module-hom-cohomology] to the right DG $B$-module $M=B$: sending a cycle $x\in B^k$ to the class of $\mu_x:b\mapsto xb$ gives an isomorphism $H^k(B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(B,B[k])$ for every $k\in\mathbf Z$. A degree-$k$ cycle $a\in A$ acts on $N={}_AB_B$ by the right $B$-linear map $b\mapsto\varphi(a)b$, which is $\mu_{\varphi(a)}$. Hence the left-action map $H^k(A)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(B,B[k])$ is the composite of $H^k(\varphi)$ with that isomorphism, and is an isomorphism for every integer $k$ by the assumed isomorphisms on cohomology. Together with Step 2 these are precisely the two hypotheses of [lem-sfb-dg-compact-bimodule-full-faithfulness], applied to $N={}_AB_B$. It follows that $L$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 09S6, first sentence of proof; Tag 09R9, lemma-tensor-with-compact-fully-faithful; the identification Hom(B,B[k]) = H^k(B) by Tags 09KY and 09KM.

proof.text: If $R(Y)\simeq0$, all cohomology groups of its underlying complex vanish. Restriction retains that complex, so $H^k(Y)=0$ for every $k$. The map $0\to Y$ is therefore a quasi-isomorphism and is inverted in $D(B,d)$, giving $Y\simeq0$. Thus $R$ has zero kernel.

source.place: Tag 09S6, third sentence of proof (the right adjoint has zero kernel).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-exact-adjoint-zero-kernel-equivalence] with $F=L$, $G=R$: exactness and the specified adjunction are Step 1, full faithfulness is Step 3, and the zero-kernel hypothesis is Step 4. Its conclusion makes this adjunction's unit $\mathrm{id}\to RL$ and counit $LR\to\mathrm{id}$ natural isomorphisms. Thus $L$ and $R$ are inverse equivalences. The exact structures and shift compatibility already supplied in Step 1 give the asserted equivalence of triangulated categories and the final compatibility clause.

lean.statement: theorem quasiIso_restriction_equivalence (A B : Algebra.{u}) [DerivedStructure A] [DerivedStructure B] (φ : A ⟶ B) (hφ : QuasiIso φ.hom) : ∃ (N : Bimod A B) (_b : AlgebraMapBimoduleModel φ N) (F : RightModule A ⥤ RightModule B) (G : RightModule B ⥤ RightModule A) (t : BalancedTensorModel N F) (r : ScalarRestrictionModel φ G) (L : Derived A ⥤ Derived B) (R : Derived B ⥤ Derived A) (α : Q A ⋙ L ⟶ F ⋙ Q B) (ρ : Q B ⋙ R ≅ G ⋙ Q A) (_sL : L.CommShift ℤ) (_sR : R.CommShift ℤ) (adj : L ⊣ R), L.IsRightKanExtension α ∧ L.IsTriangulated ∧ R.IsTriangulated ∧ adj.CommShift ℤ ∧ IsIso adj.unit ∧ IsIso adj.counit ∧ L.IsEquivalence ∧ R.IsEquivalence ∧ (∀ (M S : RightModule A) (e : ShiftComparison A 1 M S), ∃ eF : ShiftComparison B 1 (F.obj M) (F.obj S), IsTensorShift N t 1 M S e eF ∧ L.map (DerivedStructure.shiftIso 1 M S e).hom ≫ (Functor.commShiftIso L (1 : ℤ)).hom.app ((Q A).obj M) ≫ (α.app M)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = α.app S ≫ (DerivedStructure.shiftIso 1 (F.obj M) (F.obj S) eF).hom) ∧ (∀ (Y S : RightModule B) (e : ShiftComparison B 1 Y S), ∃ eG : ShiftComparison A 1 (G.obj Y) (G.obj S), eG.iso.hom ≫ (r.underlyingIso.hom.app Y)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = r.underlyingIso.hom.app S ≫ e.iso.hom ∧ R.map (DerivedStructure.shiftIso 1 Y S e).hom ≫ (Functor.commShiftIso R (1 : ℤ)).hom.app ((Q B).obj Y) ≫ (ρ.hom.app Y)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = ρ.hom.app S ≫ (DerivedStructure.shiftIso 1 (G.obj Y) (G.obj S) eG).hom)
